entries.proposition: Trio exome sequencing in two independent infantile spasms families identified two de novo variants in exon 6 of CSNK1A1 (a missense and a six-base deletion, per the Results). The quote carries the identification in two families; that the variants cause infantile spasms is the authors' interpretation and rests on HEK-293T assays and two patients, not on the exome result alone.

entries.proposition: Only the missense variant lowered CSNK1A1 mRNA and protein in the overexpression assay; the deletion did not.
entries.snippet: The results of qPCR and Western blot assays demonstrated that Mut remarkably reduced CSNK1A1 gene expression on both mRNA and protein level. However, no significant difference was observed between WT and Del despite the slight decreasing trend (Fig. 2F–H).

entries.snippet: The results of immunoprecipitation indicated that, in both Mut and Del, the interaction between CSNK1A1 and β-catenin was considerably decreased (Fig. 3E).

entries.proposition: Intracellular beta-catenin was strongly raised in cells expressing either variant, with more remaining in Mut (missense) than in Del cells; the wild-type comparator is the WT lane of Fig 3G (entry 15) and the Methods, not this quote.
entries.snippet: Moreover, the intracellular level of β-catenin was strongly enhanced in both variants (Fig. 3F and G), suggesting that the β-catenin degradation complex failed to control the concentration of β-catenin when the Wnt/β-catenin pathway was deactivated. Noticeably, more β-catenin remained in Mut cells than in Del cells.

entries.proposition: The authors declare the model limits: small sample and in vitro only, mechanism incomplete.
entries.snippet: Firstly, the sample size, although carefully selected, is relatively small. This may limit the statistical power to detect subtle associations between the gene variants and IS, and the results may not be fully representative of the entire ISS patient population. In vitro experiments, while providing valuable insights into the cellular and molecular mechanisms, cannot fully recapitulate the complex physiological environment of the human body. Finally, our understanding of the underlying mechanisms through which CSNK1A1 gene variants lead to ISS is still incomplete.

contradicts_locator.what_changed: Quote widened to the three limitation sentences (sample size, in vitro, incomplete mechanism); proposition unchanged.

entries.proposition: Fig 1A-B (embedded raster): pedigrees show Family 1 with a single affected child and Family 2 with an affected son and unaffected brother. The Family_1 proband trace in 1B shows overlapping peaks over a multi-base stretch after the junction, whose parental sequence contains GTATGT (the reverse complement of the deleted ACATAC) , and the Family_2 proband trace a single-base change G where the parents have C. The traces therefore fit Family_1 = deletion and Family_2 = missense, the OPPOSITE of the Results text, which assigns the missense (Mut, c.646G>C) to patient 1 and the deletion (Del, c.599_604delACATAC) to patient 2, and whose Discussion builds on that assignment (the missense, "patient one suffered more serious clinical outcomes"). The panel carries no variant labels and no position axis, so the "~255" position cannot be checked. UNRESOLVED source-internal conflict: neither assignment is adopted here, and every genotype-phenotype statement of the paper rests on the text assignment.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation — pixels cannot be quote-matched] Family_1 P trace overlapping peaks after position ~255; Family_2 P trace single base G where parents C

contradicts_locator.what_changed: Auditor SUPPORTED the reading but pointed out what it means: the traces fit the opposite family-to-variant assignment from the text and the position cannot be checked. Proposition now states an unresolved source-internal conflict instead of a pending adjudication.
